Obj. 5. Si Christi mors sit beneficium ex ordinatione Dei omnibus et singulis applicabile, tum dicendum est Christum satisfecisse pro peccatis totius humani generis: At hoc defendi non potest, ut interim minime labefactemus justitiam Divinam: Siquidem justitiae ratio non patitur ut bis in idem peccatum vindicetur. Fac igitur Christi mortem esse lytron quo satisfactum fuit Deo pro peccatis humani generis, quomodo ob eadem peccata hi homines a justitia Dei conveniri possunt et poenis aeternis cruciari?

Sol. Quod attinet ad Majorem, putamus ejus consequentiam tuto posse concedi. Christum enim satisfecisse pro peccatis humani generis, vel omnium hominum, intrepide afferunt orthodoxi Patres. Sic Eusebius, Demonstr. Evang. lib. 1. in praefat. Oportebat Agnum Dei pro reliquis cognatis agnis et pro omni humano genere victimam offerre. Sic Nazianzenus, Christus hostia totius mundi nunquam intermoritura expiatio est, Orat. 2. in Pasch. Sic denique (ut caeteros mittam) Cyrillus, Catech. 13. Eandem loquendi formulam Ecclesia nostra Anglicana passim usurpat in Articulis religionis, Artic. 15. 31. et alibi. Imo ita loquuntur et illi qui hanc mortem Christi vel maxime conantur restringere. Allatum fuit antea a nobis testimonium reverendi Parei Theologi Heidelbergensis, qui ultro fatetur in Judicio exhib. Synod. Dordrecht. Causam et materiam passionis Christi fuisse sensum sive sustinentiam irae Dei, peccato non aliquorum hominum sed universi generis humani concitatae. Paulo post, Universitatis peccati et irae Dei adversus illud a Christo toleratae affirmatur. Neque hoc absonum videri debet, cum haec universalis redemtio, satisfactio sive expiatio morte Christi peracta nihil aliud inferat quam universalem causam salutis humano generi Divina ordinatione stabilitam et indultam esse, cujus beneficio omnes et singuli frui possunt, mediante fide per Evangelium requisita. Appellamus igitur Christum mundi Redemtorem, atque docemus illum satisfecisse pro peccatis non aliquorum hominum sed totius mundi, non quod soluto hoc pretio pro peccatis hujus generis omnes et singuli sunt illico a captivitate et morte liberandi, sed quod virtute hujus pretii persoluti omnes et singuli possunt et debent a morte liberari, et de facto sunt liberandi, juxta pacti Evangelici tenorem, id est, si resipiscant ac credant in hunc Redemtorem. Quod porro urgetur, Esse contra justitiam accipere satisfactionem vel lytron pro peccatis universi humani generis, et tamen non omnes liberare a poenis peccatorum suorum, sed multos non obstante hac satisfactione aeternis cruciatibus adjudicare; ad hoc respondeo, Esset hoc quidem iniquissimum, si nos de nostro hoc pretium Deo persolvissemus, vel si Fidejussor noster Jesus Christus sanguinem suum tanquam pretium satisfactorium ita Deo obtulisset in redemtionem humani generis ut nulla alia conditione interveniente omnes homines ipso facto oblationis statim absolverentur, vel ipse Deus pactus fuisset cum Christo moriente, velle se omnibus et singulis fidem infundere, caeteraque omnia donare quae spectant ad infallibilem hujus hostiae pro humano genere oblatae applicationem: Sed cum ipse Deus de suo hoc pretium sibi persolvendum curaverit, penes illum fuit conditiones annectere, quibus praestitis haec mors cuivis homini esset fructuosa, minime praestitis quemvis hominem nihil juvaret. Nulla igitur injuria fit illis hominibus qui puniuntur a Deo post acceptatum lytron pro peccatis humani generis, quia ipsi nihil Deo exhibuerunt in satisfactionem pro peccatis suis, nec praestiterunt illam conditionem absque qua praestita noluit Deus ut hoc pretium satisfactorium cederet in bonum ullius personae singularis. Porro, nec Christo Mediatori hoc injuriosum censeri debet: Nam ipse sic mori voluit pro omnibus, et pro omnibus pretium redemtionis Patri numerare, ut interim non omnes et singulos quocunque modo, sed omnes ac singulos simulac crederent in eum, a reatu suorum peccatorum absolvi voluerit. Denique Christus pro expiandis mundi peccatis offerens sese in sacrificium Deo Patri, submisit tamen Patris beneplacito liberam distributionem et applicationem meritorum suorum, neque pactum ullum initum est inter Patrem et Filium, quo Deus tenetur efficere ut haec mors Christi, quae est ex ordinatione Dei omnibus applicabilis sub conditione fidei, fiat omnibus applicata per donationem fidei. Non ergo debemus negare oblationem Christi semel factam esse perfectam satisfactionem pro peccatis non aliquorum hominum solummodo sed omnium; ita tamen ut is qui simpliciter pro omnibus mortuus dicatur, ex morte sua remissionem peccatorum et salutem conditionaliter promittat et praestiturus sit solis credentibus. Similitudine haec omnia illustremus: Cogitate innumeros homines ob ingens debitum in carcerem a Rege aliquo conjectos; vel ob crimen laesae Majestatis capite damnatos; ipsum autem Regem procurare ut filius suus ad extremum assem hoc totum debitum dispungat, vel pro istis proditoribus se reum supponat, poenasque omnibus debitas sustineat, promulgata ab utroque tamen hac lege Neminem absolvendum aut liberandum esse extra eos solos qui hunc Regis Filium pro Domino suo legitimo agnoscere, illique inservire volunt. Hisce ita constitutis, quaero; si non liberentur qui perstant immorigeri et in filium Regis rebelles, nunquid injustitiae crimen incuratur ex eo quod post lytron hoc persolutum debita tamen sua a multis exigantur, aut post poenas a filio toleratas in hosce rebelles nihilominus vindicetur? Nullo modo: quia justi pretii persolutio ac poenarum debitarum toleratio ordinata quidem fuit ad remissionem cuivis impetrandam sub conditione obedientiae, et non aliter. Non addam plura: praesenti nostro instituto facile erit haec omnia accommodare.
english: Obj. 5. If Christ's death is a benefit applicable to all and each by God's ordination, then it must be said that Christ satisfied for the sins of the whole human race. But this cannot be defended without meantime undermining Divine justice: for the reason of justice does not suffer the same sin to be punished twice. Grant then that Christ's death is the lytron by which satisfaction was made to God for the sins of the human race — how can these human beings still be summoned by God's justice for the same sins and tormented with eternal punishments?

Sol. As to the Major, we judge its consequence can safely be conceded. For that Christ satisfied for the sins of the human race, or of all human beings, the orthodox Fathers boldly assert. So Eusebius, Demonstration of the Gospel, book 1, in the preface: It was fitting that the Lamb of God offer himself a victim for the remaining kindred lambs and for the whole human race. So Nazianzen: Christ is the sacrifice of the whole world, an expiation never to die, Oration 2 on Easter. So finally (to omit the rest) Cyril, Catechesis 13. The same manner of speaking our Anglican Church everywhere uses in the Articles of Religion, Articles 15 and 31, and elsewhere. Indeed even those who most strive to restrict this death of Christ speak thus. We cited earlier the testimony of the reverend Pareus, Heidelberg theologian, who freely confesses in the Judgment exhibited to the Synod of Dort that the cause and matter of Christ's passion was the sense or endurance of the wrath of God, stirred up by the sin not of some human beings but of the universal human race. A little later: the universality of sin and of the wrath of God against it, endured by Christ, is affirmed. Nor should this seem dissonant, since this universal redemption, satisfaction, or expiation accomplished by Christ's death imports nothing else than that a universal cause of salvation has been established and granted to the human race by Divine ordination, by whose benefit all and each can enjoy, through the faith required by the Gospel. We therefore call Christ the Redeemer of the world, and teach that he satisfied for the sins not of some human beings but of the whole world — not because, this price being paid for the sins of this race, all and each are immediately to be freed from captivity and death, but because by the virtue of this price paid all and each can and ought to be freed from death, and in fact are to be freed, according to the tenor of the Gospel pact, that is, if they repent and believe in this Redeemer. As to what is further urged — that it is against justice to accept satisfaction or a lytron for the sins of the universal human race, and yet not free all from the punishments of their sins, but adjudge many to eternal torments notwithstanding this satisfaction — to this I answer: This would indeed be most iniquitous if we had paid this price to God from our own, or if our Surety Jesus Christ had so offered his blood to God as a satisfactory price for the redemption of the human race that, no other condition intervening, all human beings would by the very fact of the oblation be immediately absolved, or if God himself had covenanted with the dying Christ that he willed to pour faith into all and each and to give all else that looks to the infallible application of this sacrifice offered for the human race. But since God himself arranged that this price from his own be paid to himself, it was in his power to attach conditions — which being fulfilled, this death would be fruitful to any human being; not being fulfilled, it would help no human being at all. No injury therefore is done to those human beings who are punished by God after the lytron for the sins of the human race has been accepted, because they themselves exhibited nothing to God in satisfaction for their sins, nor fulfilled that condition without which God was unwilling that this satisfactory price should turn to the good of any singular person. Further, neither should this be judged injurious to Christ the Mediator: for he so willed to die for all, and to number the price of redemption to the Father for all, that meanwhile he willed not all and each in any way whatever, but all and each as soon as they believed in him, to be absolved from the guilt of their sins. Finally Christ, offering himself in sacrifice to God the Father for expiating the world's sins, yet submitted to the Father's good pleasure the free distribution and application of his merits, and no pact was entered between Father and Son by which God is bound to effect that this death of Christ, which by God's ordination is applicable to all under the condition of faith, become applied to all through the gift of faith. We must not therefore deny that Christ's oblation once made is a perfect satisfaction for the sins not of some human beings only but of all — yet so that he who is said simply to have died for all conditionally promises from his death remission of sins and salvation, and will perform it, only to believers. Let us illustrate all this by a likeness: Think of countless human beings cast into prison by some King for an enormous debt, or condemned to death for the crime of high treason; and the King himself procuring that his son wipe out this whole debt to the last farthing, or put himself as guilty for those traitors and endure the punishments owed by all — yet with this law promulgated by both: that none is to be absolved or freed except those alone who will acknowledge this King's Son as their lawful Lord and serve him. These things being so established, I ask: if those are not freed who persist disobedient and rebellious against the King's son, is the crime of injustice incurred because after this lytron paid their debts are nonetheless exacted from many, or after the punishments endured by the son vengeance is nevertheless taken on these rebels? By no means: because the payment of a just price and the enduring of due punishments was indeed ordained to obtain remission for anyone under the condition of obedience, and not otherwise. I will not add more: it will be easy to accommodate all this to our present purpose.

Obj. 6. Nullum medium potest inveniri aut excogitari inter sufficientiam pretii et realem applicationem ejusdem: Qui ergo realem applicationem mortis Christi omnibus factam negant, non debent ulterius progredi quam ut ponant sufficientiam hujus pretii pro omnibus: supra quam quisquis vult aliquid ponere, cogitur necessario realem applicationem ejusdem omnibus concedere: Jam vero qui constituunt hanc mortem Christi ex ordinatione Dei omnibus ad salutem applicabilem, videntur inter valorem sufficientem et actualem efficaciam medium quoddam dare. At quale tandem illud erit? aut ubi reperietur? Non potest esse efficientia aliqua ad omnes et singulos homines indifferenter spectans, et in illis per mortem Christi causata; quia tale effectum assignari nequit. Neque possumus vi mortis Christi in ipso Deo ponere sive impetrationem quandam remissionis peccatorum ad omnes extensam, sive intentionem applicationis. Restat igitur ut ultra sufficientiam pretii nihil ponamus, quod omnes spectet, ex morte Christi redundare.

Sol. Ut huic objectioni occuratur, inprimis videndum est qualem sufficientiam intelligant qui ita ratiocinantur, et retinent interim hanc Scholasticorum distinctionem, Christum pro omnibus mortuum sufficienter, pro electis efficaciter. Christum ergo pro omnibus mortuum sufficienter, sic intelligunt; Mors Christi est sufficiens ad omnes redimendos, sed pro omnibus mori noluit: mors Christi est in se et valore suo intrinseco sufficiens lytron pro omnibus, sed pro omnibus non fuit persolutum. At Scholasticis nunquam in mentem venit ex hypothesi tantum defendere hanc sufficientiam, et absolute negare Christum pro omnibus mortuum. Neque potest facile explicari quomodo sine aperta contradictione affirmaretur Christus pro omnibus mortuus vel oblatus sufficienter, et interim pro multis omnino negetur mori aut offerri voluisse. Quoad hosce igitur qui talem solummodo hypotheticam oblationem et sufficientiam admittunt in morte Christi, si ad omnes referatur, respondeo, Medium assignari posse et debere inter meram istam sufficientiam pretii et realem applicationem ejusdem. Nam ordinatio Dei in Evangelio patefacta, juxta quam haec mors Christi proponitur ut percipienda cuivis resipiscenti et credenti, probat medium quoddam inter illam sufficientiam et actualem applicationem esse constitutum. In hac etenim ordinatione Dei, juxta quam mors Christi statuitur et proponitur ut causa salutis cuivis viatori per fidem applicabilis, continetur minus quam in reali applicatione, continetur tamen quoddam amplius quam in mera et nuda rei sufficientia per se considerata, exclusa hac ordinatione conditionali, ad quemlibet humanae naturae participem spectante. Est igitur hoc illud ipsum medium quod assignari posse negarant adversarii; sed adhuc urgent et quaerunt, quid sit illud in quo productum hoc quasi medium, quod nudam sufficientiam superat, et tamen ad realem applicationem non attingit. Respondeo, Ut non sit actus aliquis, ad omnes et singulos indifferenter spectans, ex morte Christi causatus, est tamen titulus ad vitam aeternam, sub conditione fidei ad omnes et singulos indifferenter spectans, in morte Christi fundatus: ut non sit in Deo impetratio remissionis, vel intentio applicationis, juxta infallibilem praedestinationis ordinem ad omnes et singulos extensa, est tamen in Deo obligatio quaedam ad remissionem, et voluntas remittendi peccata, et vitam conferendi, extensa ad omnes et singulos, juxta tenorem Evangelicae promissionis. Sed pluribus jam supersedeo, quia cum ad proximam thesin ventum fuerit, de hac ipsa re ex instituto magis copiose disseremus.
english: Obj. 6. No middle can be found or devised between the sufficiency of the price and its real application. Those therefore who deny that a real application of Christ's death has been made to all ought not to proceed further than to posit the sufficiency of this price for all: above which whoever wishes to posit anything is necessarily compelled to concede a real application of the same to all. But now those who constitute this death of Christ as applicable to all unto salvation by God's ordination seem to give some middle between sufficient value and actual efficacy. But of what sort, pray, will that be? or where will it be found? It cannot be some efficiency looking indifferently to all and each human being and caused in them by Christ's death; because such an effect cannot be assigned. Nor can we, by virtue of Christ's death, place in God himself either some impetration of remission of sins extended to all, or an intention of application. It remains therefore that beyond the sufficiency of the price we posit nothing that looks to all as overflowing from Christ's death.

Sol. That this objection may be met, it must first be seen what sufficiency they understand who so reason, and meanwhile retain this distinction of the Scholastics — that Christ died sufficiently for all, efficaciously for the elect. They therefore understand Christ to have died sufficiently for all thus: Christ's death is sufficient to redeem all, but he was unwilling to die for all; Christ's death is in itself and in its intrinsic value a sufficient lytron for all, but it was not paid for all. But it never entered the Scholastics' mind to defend this sufficiency only hypothetically and absolutely to deny that Christ died for all. Nor can it easily be explained how without open contradiction it could be affirmed that Christ died or was offered sufficiently for all, and meanwhile be denied that he willed to die or be offered for many at all. As to those therefore who admit only such a hypothetical oblation and sufficiency in Christ's death, if it be referred to all, I answer that a middle can and ought to be assigned between that bare sufficiency of the price and its real application. For God's ordination revealed in the Gospel, according to which this death of Christ is proposed as to be received by any who repent and believe, proves that some middle has been constituted between that sufficiency and actual application. For in this ordination of God, according to which Christ's death is established and proposed as a cause of salvation applicable by faith to any wayfarer, there is contained less than in real application, yet there is contained something fuller than in the mere and bare sufficiency of the thing considered in itself, this conditional ordination looking to any sharer in human nature being excluded. This therefore is that very middle which the adversaries denied could be assigned; but they still urge and ask what that is in which this quasi-middle is produced, which surpasses bare sufficiency and yet does not reach real application. I answer: Though there is not some act looking indifferently to all and each, caused from Christ's death, yet there is a title to eternal life, looking indifferently to all and each under the condition of faith, founded in Christ's death; though there is not in God an impetration of remission, or an intention of application, extended to all and each according to the infallible order of predestination, yet there is in God a certain obligation to remission, and a will to remit sins and to confer life, extended to all and each according to the tenor of the Gospel promise. But I now forbear more, because when we come to the next thesis we shall treat of this very matter more copiously by design.

Obj. 7. Patris voluntas, Filii oblatio, Spiritus sancti salutaris operatio aeque late patent, easdemque personas respiciunt: At Patris voluntas est servare solos electos; et Spiritus, infundendo fidem ac donando perseverantiam, de facto servat solos electos: Ergo mors sive oblatio Christi non est extendenda nisi ad solos electos, atque idcirco non debet considerari ut remedium ex ordinatione Dei omnibus et singulis applicabile ad salutem.

Sol. Si de voluntate Dei praedestinantis, quae semper cum infallibilitate eventus conjuncta est, et de speciali illa operatione Spiritus sanctificantis, quae huic decreto exsequendo inservit, intelligatur Major propositio, dico non esse absolute veram: Nam mors Christi sive oblatio, aliquo modo respicit quasdam personas, quas praedestinatio non complectitur. Praedestinatio est arcanum Dei decretum, quo apud se ab aeterno praestituit quibus ex infinito merito mortis Christi velit gratiam efficacem et vitam aeternam infallibiliter donare: at oblatio Christi in cruce est commune humano generi indultum beneficium, cujus virtute quilibet, modo id vera fide amplectatur, potest vitam aeternam juxta revelatam in Evangelio Dei voluntatem sibi vendicare. Sic loquitur ipse Christus Johann. iii. 14, 15. Sicut Moses extulit serpentem in deserto, ita extolli oportet Filium hominis ut quisquis credat in eum non pereat, sed habeat vitam aeternam. Quamvis igitur praedestinatio Dei et, quae ex illa dependet, efficax vocatio, neminem non-electum complectitur, tamen sicut oblatio Christi in Evangelio, ita et oblatio Christi in cruce, latius patet, et cuilibet homini tam applicabilis quam annunciabilis est, et fiet salutifera cuilibet modo credat; Deo interim relicta arcana sua voluntate, juxta quam statuit misericorditer in quibusdam efficere ut credant, alios innatae suae duritiei permittere, atque in illis haud efficere ut credant. Tandem et illud addo, fuisse in ipso Christo voluntatem juxta quam voluit mortem suam ad omnes et singulos spectare, fuisse etiam juxta quam ad solos electos voluit eandem pertinere. Voluit illam spectare ad omnes Adami posteros servandos, atque de facto omnes servare, modo eam vera fide amplecterentur: voluit illam ad solos electos ita pertinere ut ex merito ejus omnia quae ad consequendam salutem spectant infallibiliter iisdem donarentur. Atque hoc sensu fatemur oblationem Christi aeque late patere atque praedestinationem Dei: De qua plura suo loco.
english: Obj. 7. The Father's will, the Son's oblation, and the Holy Spirit's saving operation are equally wide, and regard the same persons. But the Father's will is to save the elect alone; and the Spirit, by infusing faith and giving perseverance, in fact saves the elect alone: therefore Christ's death or oblation is not to be extended except to the elect alone, and for that reason ought not to be considered as a remedy applicable to all and each unto salvation by God's ordination.

Sol. If the Major proposition is understood of the will of the predestinating God, which is always joined with infallibility of event, and of that special operation of the sanctifying Spirit which serves the execution of this decree, I say it is not absolutely true: for Christ's death or oblation somehow regards certain persons whom predestination does not embrace. Predestination is God's secret decree, by which he determined with himself from eternity to whom from the infinite merit of Christ's death he wills to give efficacious grace and eternal life infallibly; but Christ's oblation on the cross is a common benefit granted to the human race, by whose virtue anyone, provided he embraces it with true faith, can claim eternal life for himself according to God's will revealed in the Gospel. So Christ himself speaks in ([[John 3:14–15 >> Bible:John 3:14]]): As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of man be lifted up, that whosoever believes in him should not perish but have eternal life. Although therefore God's predestination and the efficacious calling that depends on it embrace no non-elect person, yet as Christ's oblation in the Gospel, so also Christ's oblation on the cross, is wider, and is as applicable to any human being as it is announcible, and will become salvific to anyone provided he believes — God's secret will meanwhile being left to him, according to which he has determined mercifully to cause some to believe, to permit others to their innate hardness, and in them not to cause that they believe. Finally I add also this: that there was in Christ himself a will according to which he willed his death to look to all and each, and also one according to which he willed the same to pertain to the elect alone. He willed it to look to all Adam's posterity to be saved, and in fact to save all, provided they embraced it with true faith; he willed it so to pertain to the elect alone that from its merit all things that look to obtaining salvation should be infallibly given them. And in this sense we confess that Christ's oblation is equally wide with God's predestination — of which more in its place.

Obj. 8. Si Christi mors ex ordinatione Dei omnibus et singulis applicabilis statuatur, tum tollitur omne discrimen electorum et non-electorum, atque doctrina praedestinationis prorsus evertitur: Si enim Christus quocunque sensu pro omnibus mortuus dicatur, quid impedit quin eodem sensu omnes et singulos homines a Deo electos pronunciemus?

Sol. Haec proficiscuntur ab ignorata electionis sive praedestinationis vera ratione. Non enim quaevis ordinatio ad salutem per qualiacunque media ponit hominem in numero electorum aut praedestinatorum, sed ordinatio per talia media quae Deus et novit et decrevit effectum salutis in homine electo infallibiliter productura. Hinc illa definitio praedestinationis apud Augustinum, De bono persever. cap. 14. Est praescientia et praeparatio beneficiorum Dei, quibus certissime liberantur quicunque liberantur. Hinc etiam illa catena Apostolica, Rom. viii. 29, 30. in qua praedestinatio inseparabili nexu cum glorificatione finali copulatur; Quos praedestinavit, hos et glorificavit. Utcunque ergo fateamur Christi mortem sub aliqua ratione ordinatam a Deo in commune remedium humani generis, et profituram omnibus sub hac conditione Evangelica, si crediderint; tamen non hinc sequitur omnes et singulos esse promiscue electos, quia Deus non decrevit omnibus et singulis illam gratiam donare ut credant, et credendo ex hac morte Christi vitam infallibiliter hauriant. Imo et illud addi potest, Licet demus non modo Christum pro omnibus fuisse mortuum, sed etiam propter hanc mortem Christi sufficientem gratiam omnibus et singulis a Deo esse praeparatam et donatam (quod tamen non tenemus) adhuc nemo ex hisce concessis recte inferret omnes homines esse promiscue electos, vel nullum esse discrimen inter electos et praeteritos. Ratio in promptu est; Quia nulla quantumvis sufficiens ordinatio mediorum ad salutem hominis procurandam arguit illum esse praedestinatum, nisi illud accesserit, ut sit infallibilis quidem ordo specialis providentiae statuens et dirigens media ordinata ad certissimam et infrustrabilem finis consecutionem. Potest hoc illustrari exemplo Angelorum et Hominum in statu naturae integrae consideratorum. Angeli omnes et singuli conditi fuerunt sufficiente gratia instructi, atque inde sufficienter ordinati ad beatitudinem obtinendam: non tamen hinc evincitur aut nullam fuisse electionem inter angelos, aut omnes fuisse indiscriminatim electos. Sic ipse Adamus in sua creatione, atque in illo posteri ejus omnes, intelliguntur sufficiente gratia donati, atque ad vitam aeternam consequendam debite instructi: neque tamen inde sequetur omnes homines fuisse electos, aut nullam dari praedestinationem. Non enim ordinatio quaelibet ad vitae aeternae consecutionem aut ponit illico hominem electum, aut negat non-electum, sed (uti dictum est) ordinatio infallibilis. Ut itaque redeamus ad id quod in manibus est; Ex Christi morte omnibus et singulis hominibus in propitiatorium sacrificium ordinata, et per fidem ad remissionem et salutem obtinendam applicabili, non consequitur tolli electionem et praeteritionem, quia posita hac communi ordinatione, et in Evangelio revelata, est insuper arcana quaedam ordinatio juxta quam praedicta Christi mors quibusdam, quorum Deus vult specialiter misereri, infallibiliter applicanda decernitur; aliis, quorum non vult illo modo misereri, non ita applicanda decernitur. Et hoc abunde sufficit ad praedestinationis et reprobationis doctrinam tuendam; quamvis Christi mortem ad omnes sensu praedicto extendamus.
english: Obj. 8. If Christ's death is set as applicable to all and each by God's ordination, then every distinction of elect and non-elect is removed, and the doctrine of predestination is utterly overturned: for if Christ is said to have died for all in any sense, what prevents our pronouncing all and each human beings elect by God in the same sense?

Sol. These things proceed from ignorance of the true reason of election or predestination. For it is not any ordination to salvation through media of whatever sort that puts a human being in the number of the elect or predestined, but an ordination through such media as God both knows and has decreed will infallibly produce the effect of salvation in the elect person. Hence that definition of predestination in Augustine, On the Gift of Perseverance, chapter 14: It is the foreknowledge and preparation of God's benefits, by which whoever are liberated are most certainly liberated. Hence also that Apostolic chain in ([[Romans 8:29–30 >> Bible:Romans 8:29]]), in which predestination is coupled by an inseparable bond with final glorification: Whom he predestined, them he also glorified. Although therefore we confess that Christ's death under some respect has been ordained by God as a common remedy of the human race, and will profit all under this Gospel condition if they have believed; yet it does not follow from this that all and each are promiscuously elect, because God has not decreed to give to all and each that grace that they may believe, and by believing draw life infallibly from this death of Christ. Indeed this also can be added: even if we grant not only that Christ died for all, but also that on account of this death of Christ sufficient grace has been prepared and given by God to all and each (which nevertheless we do not hold), still no one would rightly infer from these concessions that all human beings are promiscuously elect, or that there is no distinction between the elect and the passed-by. The reason is ready at hand: because no however sufficient ordination of media to procure a human being's salvation argues that he is predestined, unless there has also accrued this — that there be indeed an infallible order of special providence establishing and directing the ordained media to the most certain and unfrustrable attainment of the end. This can be illustrated by the example of Angels and of Human beings considered in the state of intact nature. All and each angels were created instructed with sufficient grace, and thence sufficiently ordained to obtaining beatitude: yet it is not thereby proved either that there was no election among the angels, or that all were indiscriminately elect. So Adam himself in his creation, and in him all his posterity, are understood to have been given sufficient grace and duly instructed for obtaining eternal life: yet it will not follow from this that all human beings were elect, or that no predestination is given. For it is not any ordination whatever to the attainment of eternal life that immediately posits a human being elect or denies a non-elect, but (as has been said) an infallible ordination. To return therefore to what is in hand: from Christ's death ordained for all and each human being as a propitiatory sacrifice, and applicable by faith to obtaining remission and salvation, it does not follow that election and preterition are removed, because, this common ordination being posited and revealed in the Gospel, there is besides a certain secret ordination according to which the aforesaid death of Christ is decreed to be applied infallibly to some, of whom God wills specially to have mercy, and not so to be applied to others, of whom he does not will to have mercy in that way. And this abundantly suffices to defend the doctrine of predestination and reprobation, though we extend Christ's death to all in the aforesaid sense.

Obj. 9. Disputant nonnulli, argumento ducto a pari, ut ipsi opinantur, hoc modo: Tam est a vero alienum, Christum ex Dei ordinatione mortuum esse pro aliquibus qui non servantur, quam servari aliquos pro quibus ex Dei ordinatione mortuus non est; At hoc absurdum est dici: Ergo et illud.

Sol. Nego parem esse utrobique rationem. Nam (quod in Schola Theologorum est receptissimum) Bonum non oritur nisi ex causis integris, malum ex quovis defectu. Salus igitur humana, quae maximum bonum est, non producitur nisi pleno concursu omnium causarum: at salutis amissio, quae malum est, posita uni aut alteri causa ad salutem hominis ordinata, evenire potest nihilominus ex defectu cujuscunque. Licet ergo sit impossibile servari aliquos homines pro quibus Christus non est mortuus, quia Christi mors est una ex illis causis ordinatis quae operantur salutem humanam; non tamen est impossibile a salute excidere quosdam pro quibus est mortuus, quia non est a Deo statutum, ut sola haec mors Christi ipso facto oblationis redderet Deum omnibus propitium, et omnes servaret, sed ut esset placamentum per fidem in sanguine ipsius, ad declarandam justitiam suam per remissionem peccatorum, Rom. iii. 25, itaque in omnes et super omnes qui credunt: non est enim distinctio, ut habetur vers. 22. Si porro quis urgeat, Cur mors Christi omnibus hominibus in remedium data defenditur, fides autem omnibus donata aut praeparata non defenditur? respondeo, Quia Scripturae clare docent Christum moriendo impetrasse omnibus et singulis hominibus hanc gratiam, ut sub conditione fidei possint jam sperare et obtinere remissionem peccatorum et salutem; at haec gratia conditionalis non posset omnibus offerri, neque ad omnes quoquo modo spectaret, nisi haec mors Christi ad omnes homines ex Dei ipsius ordinatione pertineret: Jam ex altera parte non defendimus fidem omnibus destinatam aut donatam, quia eadem sacra Scriptura, quae proponit mortem Christi ut beneficium omnibus indultum, et cuivis per fidem applicabile, non facit hanc fidem beneficium omnibus promissum aut datum, sed ex peculiari decreto electionis derivatum. His adde, ipsum Mediatorem, qui se in sacrificium Deo obtulit pro expiandis mundi peccatis, obtinuisse a Deo ut omnes et singuli qui in eum credituri essent a peccatis absolverentur, atque hactenus voluisse hoc lytron pro omnibus persolvere: sed non applicuisse omnibus meritum mortis suae, neque obtinuisse a Deo ut omnes infallibiliter fidem et salutem consequerentur. Atque hic se aperit arcanum electionis, quod universalitatem oblationis et veritatem Evangelicae promissionis non debet evertere aut enervare.
english: Obj. 9. Some dispute, by an argument drawn from parity, as they think, in this way: It is as far from the truth that Christ by God's ordination died for some who are not saved, as that some are saved for whom by God's ordination he did not die; But this is absurd to say: Therefore that also.

Sol. I deny that the reason is equal on both sides. For (what is most received in the School of Theologians) Good does not arise except from complete causes, evil from any defect whatever. Human salvation, therefore, which is the greatest good, is not produced except by the full concurrence of all causes: but the loss of salvation, which is an evil, once one or another cause ordained to a human being's salvation is in place, can nevertheless occur from the defect of any. Although therefore it is impossible that some human beings be saved for whom Christ did not die, because Christ's death is one of those ordained causes which work human salvation; yet it is not impossible that some for whom he did die fall away from salvation, because it was not established by God that this death of Christ alone by the very fact of offering should render God propitious to all and save all, but that it should be a propitiation through faith in his blood, for the declaring of his righteousness through the remission of sins ([[Romans 3:25 >> Bible:Romans 3:25]]), and so upon all and over all who believe: for there is no distinction, as is had in verse 22. If further someone presses, Why is Christ's death defended as given to all human beings as a remedy, but faith given or prepared for all is not defended? I answer, Because the Scriptures clearly teach that Christ by dying obtained for all and each human being this grace, that under the condition of faith they can now hope for and obtain remission of sins and salvation; but this conditional grace could not be offered to all, nor would it look in any way to all, unless this death of Christ belonged to all human beings by God's own ordination: Now on the other side we do not defend faith as destined or given to all, because the same sacred Scripture which proposes Christ's death as a benefit granted to all, and applicable to anyone through faith, does not make this faith a benefit promised or given to all, but derived from the peculiar decree of election. Add to these that the Mediator himself, who offered himself to God as a sacrifice for expiating the world's sins, obtained from God that all and each who would believe in him should be absolved from sins, and thus far willed to pay this lytron for all: but he did not apply to all the merit of his death, nor obtain from God that all should infallibly follow faith and salvation. And here the secret of election opens, which ought not to overturn or weaken the universality of the offering and the truth of the Gospel promise.

Obj. 10. Si Christi mors a nobis sit concipienda ut remedium omnibus hominibus applicabile, tum sacrae Scripturae non restringerent ipsam dationem Filii ad solos credentes: At illae non fructum tantummodo sive applicationem realem, sed ipsam dationem Filii solis fidelibus vendicant. Johann. iii. 16. Sic Deus dilexit mundum, ut dederit Filium suum unigenitum, ut quicunque credit in eum non pereat, sed habeat vitam aeternam. Quod datur hominibus sub conditione, sublata illa conditione nulli datum intelligitur. Cum igitur haec conditio credendi a solis electis impleatur, consequens est ut pro illis solis Christum fuisse oblatum dicamus: Ac proinde haec oblatio, sive mors Christi, non est ex ordinatione Dei remedium vel lytron omnibus et singulis hominibus applicabile.

Sol. Possumus duplicem Christi Dationem sive oblationem considerare. Prior illa est, qua Deo Patri in ara crucis Datus sive oblatus intelligitur ad tollenda mundi peccata: de qua Apostolus, 1 Tim. ii. 6. Unus est Deus; unus Mediator Dei et hominum, homo Christus Jesus, qui semetipsum dedit redemtionis pretium pro omnibus, Deo scilicet Patri suo, ut clarius exprimitur Ephes. v. 2. Tradidit semetipsum pro nobis oblationem et hostiam Deo, etc. Haec oblatio est fundamentum posterioris cujusdam oblationis, qua hominibus offertur in Evangelio, ut per fidem apprehensus vitam aeternam illis ex merito hujus sacrificii largiatur; De hac oblatione loquitur idem Apostolus, Justificamur gratis per redemtionem factam in Jesu Christo: Quem proposuit Deus ut esset placamentum per fidem in sanguine ipsius, etc. Si priorem oblationem respiciamus, nego Christum se obtulisse hostiam vel dedisse in lytron Deo Patri pro expiandis mundi peccatis sub conditione fidei humanae, quasi sub hac formula, Ego meipsum tibi offero in hostiam pro peccatis humani generis, modo in Me crediderit. Sed simpliciter haud conditionaliter se Deo Patri obtulit. Et hoc quidem inde evincitur, quod ipse Pater, juxta cujus voluntatem Filius se obtulit in sacrificium, non constituit apud se dare Redemtorem mundo sub hac hypothesi, Si mundus crederet; sed Deus dedit Filium suum mundo, et Filius dedit semetipsum Patri lytron pro peccatis mundi tollendis, gratuito et absolute. Conditio quidem annexa est in praedicatione Evangelica, non ipsi dationi, sed vitae aeternae ex rei datae fructuosa applicatione secuturae. Quod igitur ad posteriorem oblationem spectat, qua Christus Deo pro hominibus oblatus jam ipsis hominibus offertur in Evangelio, nego etiam hypotheticam et conditionalem oblationem sive dationem Christi vel ex hac praedicatione Evangelica esse cogitandam. Non enim dixit Servator in loco supra allegato, Sic Deus dilexit mundum ut dederit Filium pro eo si crederet: sed postquam ex Dei philanthropia absolute datum pronunciasset omnibus, ostendit non tamen profuturum omnibus ad vitam aeternam absolute et simpliciter, sed conditionaliter, omnibus nempe, si crediderint, vel omnibus qui crediderint. Nos etiam si quando infidelibus, puta Indis aut Americanis, praedicaremus Evangelium, non ita eos instituere aggrederemur, Christus Dei Filius pro quibusdam ex vobis mortuus est qui in eum sunt credituri, pro aliis minime; sed, Christus pro tollendis totius mundi peccatis mortuus est, et dedit semetipsum lytron Deo Patri, ita tamen ut nec Christus qui obtulit semetipsum redemtionis pretium pro omnibus, nec Deus Pater cui oblatus est, velit quenquam vestrum prius a peccatis suis liberari quam credat in Deum, et in illum quem misit Jesum Christum. Quod itaque ultimo in loco urgetur, Quod sub conditione fidei datum aut promissum intelligitur, hac conditione minime praestita, nemini datum aut promissum supponitur; atque idcirco Christus solis electis, qui conditionem praestant, datus vere affirmatur; ad hoc respondeo, Nusquam in Scripturis Christum, Christive mortem sive sacrificium, sub conditione legimus humano generi datum aut promissum, quamvis salus seu vita aeterna ubique sub conditione fidei danda promittitur. Quanquam et illud addi potest, Etiam rem sub conditione promissam aliquo modo ad eos spectasse qui conditionem nunquam implent, nimirum quoad jus vendicandi promissum beneficium, si implevissent. Quod innuere videtur ipse Christus Johann. iii. 18, Ubi docet incredulos condemnari, quia non crediderunt in nomen unigeniti Filii Dei. Habuerunt igitur mortem Filii Dei sibi applicabilem etiam qui non crediderunt, quamvis non habuerunt eandem applicatam, quia non crediderunt. Atque hanc ob causam soli electi vitam in morte Christi inveniunt, quia Deo illorum miserante soli credunt.
english: Obj. 10. If Christ's death is to be conceived by us as a remedy applicable to all human beings, then the sacred Scriptures would not restrict the very giving of the Son to believers alone: But they claim for the faithful alone not only the fruit or real application, but the very giving of the Son. ([[John 3:16 >> Bible:John 3:16]]): So God loved the world, that he gave his only-begotten Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life. What is given to human beings under a condition, that condition being removed, is understood as given to no one. Since therefore this condition of believing is fulfilled by the elect alone, it follows that we should say Christ was offered for them alone: And accordingly this offering, or Christ's death, is not by God's ordination a remedy or lytron applicable to all and each human being.

Sol. We can consider a twofold Giving or offering of Christ. The prior is that by which he is understood as Given or offered to God the Father on the altar of the cross for taking away the world's sins: of which the Apostle, ([[1 Timothy 2:6 >> Bible:1 Timothy 2:6]]): There is one God; one Mediator of God and human beings, the human being Christ Jesus, who gave himself a ransom-price of redemption for all, namely to God his Father, as is more clearly expressed in ([[Ephesians 5:2 >> Bible:Ephesians 5:2]]): He delivered himself for us an offering and sacrifice to God, etc. This offering is the foundation of a certain later offering, by which he is offered to human beings in the Gospel, that being grasped by faith he may bestow eternal life on them from the merit of this sacrifice; Of this offering the same Apostle speaks, We are justified freely through the redemption made in Jesus Christ: Whom God set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, etc. If we look to the prior offering, I deny that Christ offered himself as a victim or gave himself as a lytron to God the Father for expiating the world's sins under the condition of human faith, as if under this formula, I offer myself to you as a victim for the sins of the human race, provided he has believed in Me. But he offered himself to God the Father simply, not conditionally. And this is proved from the fact that the Father himself, according to whose will the Son offered himself in sacrifice, did not establish with himself to give a Redeemer to the world under this hypothesis, If the world should believe; but God gave his Son to the world, and the Son gave himself to the Father as a lytron for taking away the world's sins, freely and absolutely. A condition indeed is annexed in Gospel preaching, not to the giving itself, but to the eternal life that will follow from the fruitful application of the thing given. As for the later offering, therefore, by which Christ offered to God for human beings is now offered to human beings themselves in the Gospel, I deny also that a hypothetical and conditional offering or giving of Christ is to be thought even from this Gospel preaching. For the Savior did not say in the place alleged above, So God loved the world that he gave the Son for it if it should believe: but after he had pronounced him given absolutely to all from God's love of humankind, he showed that he would not nevertheless profit all unto eternal life absolutely and simply, but conditionally, namely all, if they have believed, or all who have believed. We too, if ever we should preach the Gospel to unbelievers, say Indians or Americans, would not set about instructing them thus, Christ the Son of God died for some of you who are going to believe in him, for others not at all; but, Christ died for taking away the sins of the whole world, and gave himself a lytron to God the Father, yet so that neither Christ who offered himself a redemption-price for all, nor God the Father to whom he was offered, wills any of you to be freed from your sins before you believe in God, and in him whom he sent, Jesus Christ. As for what is urged last, That what is understood as given or promised under the condition of faith, that condition not being performed, is supposed given or promised to no one; and therefore Christ is truly affirmed given to the elect alone, who perform the condition; to this I answer, Nowhere in the Scriptures do we read that Christ, or Christ's death or sacrifice, was given or promised to the human race under a condition, although salvation or eternal life is everywhere promised to be given under the condition of faith. Although this too can be added, That even a thing promised under a condition somehow looked to those who never fulfill the condition, namely as to the right of claiming the promised benefit if they had fulfilled it. Which Christ himself seems to hint at in ([[John 3:18 >> Bible:John 3:18]]), Where he teaches that unbelievers are condemned, because they did not believe in the name of the only-begotten Son of God. They therefore had the death of the Son of God applicable to themselves even who did not believe, although they did not have it applied, because they did not believe. And for this reason the elect alone find life in Christ's death, because by God pitying them they alone believe.

Obj. 11. Christi mors non est applicabilis illis pro quibus non est mortuus sive oblatus: At innumeri homines sunt pro quibus non est mortuus sive oblatus, nempe illi omnes qui minime conscripti fuerunt in albo electorum ante jacta mundi fundamenta. Exinde Minorem confirmare conantur, quod Apostolus diserte afferat, Deum omnia velle gratificari illis pro quibus Filius mortuus est, Rom. viii. 32. Qui proprio Filio non pepercit, sed pro nobis omnibus tradidit eum, quomodo non etiam cum eo omnia nobis gratificabitur? Verum omnia non gratificatur omnibus: Ergo Christus non est pro omnibus mortuus: Ergo mors ejus non est omnibus applicabilis.

Sol. Lubenter concedo Christi mortem nullo vero sensu dici posse applicabilem illis, pro quibus Deus nullatenus eum mori voluit. Mors enim Christi non est remedium applicabile ad expianda peccata cujuspiam nisi ex ordinatione et acceptatione Dei. Atque hanc ob causam, licet lytron a Christo persolutum Deo Patri sit in se sufficientis et superabundantis valoris ad redimenda peccata non hominum modo sed angelorum lapsorum, tamen propter defectum ordinationis et acceptationis quoad angelos, vere negamus Christum pro illis ullo modo mortuum dici oportere. De hominibus etiam illis idem statuendum esset, si qui essent propter eundem defectum ordinationis et acceptationis Divinae ab omni possibilitate dictae redemtionis alieni et exclusi. Sed uti dictum est, concessa Majore, ad Minorem accedamus. Respondeo igitur, Neminem esse ejusdem humanae naturae participem quam Redemtor assumere dignatus est, pro quo Christus non tradiderit semetipsum redemtionis pretium applicabile ex ordinatione et acceptatione Dei ad remissionem peccatorum obtinendam per fidem in sanguine ipsius. Neque Apostolus nobis contradicit, cujus totus ille discursus, Rom. viii, non spectat ad consolandos quosvis homines in quolibet statu positos, sed electos; nec electos simpliciter, sed electos jam vocatos, justificatos, sanctificatos, id est, ut idem loquitur, Col. i. 13, jam liberatos a potestate tenebrarum, et translatos in regnum Filii sibi dilecti. Neque simpliciter et universe affirmat Deum omnia omnibus hominibus gratificari pro quibus Christus mortuus est, sed omnibus illis de quibus praesens sermo instituitur, id est, omnibus praedestinatis in Christum credentibus, pro quibus non solummodo mortuus est Christus, sed quibus insuper jam datus est Christus speciali modo, hoc est, unitus, et cum infinito thesauro meritorum suorum communicatus. Est itaque efficax argumentum hoc consolatorium Apostoli a morte Christi petitum, sed si ad eos et eatenus accommodatur, ad quos et quatenus illud ab Apostolo fuit accommodatum: nempe hoc modo, Tu qui ex vocatione tua efficaci, justificatione et sanctificatione jam agnoscere et sentire potes te esse praedestinatum, et Deum pro te specialiter et efficaciter redimendo Filium suum non modo sibi oblatum, sed etiam tibi communicatum voluisse, qui potes non confidere illum de caetero reliqua omnia ad salutem consummandam necessaria tibi gratificaturum? Verum si ad quoslibet homines, seclusa consideratione praedestinationis, vocationis, justificationis, quis velit praedictam rationem adhibere, hoc modo, Christus pro vobis mortuus est, vel Christus dedit se lytron sive hostiam Deo pro peccatis vestris expiandis, ergo et Deus vobis omnia gratificabitur, dico, illum extra suos limites praeter mentem Apostoli hoc argumentum trahere; qui illud arctavit ad certas personas, nempe praedestinatos, easdemque in certo statu jam positas, scilicet justificationis et adoptionis.
english: Obj. 11. Christ's death is not applicable to those for whom he did not die or was not offered: But there are countless human beings for whom he did not die or was not offered, namely all those who were not enrolled in the register of the elect before the foundations of the world were laid. From this they try to confirm the Minor, because the Apostle expressly asserts that God wills to grant all things to those for whom the Son died, ([[Romans 8:32 >> Bible:Romans 8:32]]): He who did not spare his own Son, but delivered him up for us all, how will he not also with him freely give us all things? But he does not freely give all things to all: Therefore Christ did not die for all: Therefore his death is not applicable to all.

Sol. I gladly grant that Christ's death can in no true sense be said applicable to those for whom God in no way willed him to die. For Christ's death is not a remedy applicable to expiating anyone's sins except by God's ordination and acceptance. And for this reason, although the lytron paid by Christ to God the Father is in itself of sufficient and superabundant value for redeeming the sins not only of human beings but of fallen angels, yet because of the defect of ordination and acceptance as to the angels, we truly deny that Christ ought to be said to have died for them in any way. The same would have to be held of those human beings too, if there were any who by the same defect of Divine ordination and acceptance were alien and excluded from every possibility of the said redemption. But as has been said, the Major being granted, let us come to the Minor. I answer therefore, That there is no one sharing the same human nature which the Redeemer deigned to assume, for whom Christ has not delivered himself as a redemption-price applicable by God's ordination and acceptance for obtaining remission of sins through faith in his blood. Nor does the Apostle contradict us, whose whole discourse in Romans 8 does not look to consoling any human beings whatever placed in any state, but the elect; nor the elect simply, but the elect already called, justified, sanctified, that is, as the same speaks in ([[Colossians 1:13 >> Bible:Colossians 1:13]]), already delivered from the power of darkness, and transferred into the kingdom of the Son of his love. Nor does he affirm simply and universally that God freely gives all things to all human beings for whom Christ died, but to all those of whom the present discourse is instituted, that is, to all the predestined believing in Christ, for whom not only did Christ die, but to whom moreover Christ has already been given in a special mode, that is, united, and communicated with the infinite treasure of his merits. This consolatory argument of the Apostle drawn from Christ's death is therefore efficacious, but if it is accommodated to those and so far, to whom and so far as it was accommodated by the Apostle: namely in this way, You who from your effectual calling, justification and sanctification can already acknowledge and feel that you are predestined, and that God in specially and effectually redeeming you willed his Son not only offered to himself, but also communicated to you, how can you not trust that he will for the rest freely give you all other things necessary for consummating salvation? But if anyone should wish to apply the aforesaid reason to any human beings whatever, setting aside consideration of predestination, calling, justification, in this way, Christ died for you, or Christ gave himself a lytron or victim to God for expiating your sins, therefore God will also freely give you all things, I say he draws this argument beyond its limits contrary to the Apostle's mind; who narrowed it to certain persons, namely the predestined, and those already placed in a certain state, namely of justification and adoption.

Obj. 12. Christus ordinatus est redemtor non ex philanthropia, sed ex eudokia speciali qua Deus electos suos specialiter complexus est ad vitam aeternam: Christi igitur mors non est lytron omnibus hominibus redimendis applicabile ex ordinatione Dei, sed solis electis destinatum.

Sol. Nego antecedens: et affirmo Deum in redemtore mittendo voluisse utrumque amorem mundo testatum reddere, nempe communem illum amorem humani generis quem philanthropian vocamus, et illum specialem atque arcanum quem eudokian appellamus. Communis amoris argumentum est, quod humano generi, id est, omnibus et singulis hominibus, hactenus prospectum voluerit, ut haberent redemtorem, per cujus satisfactionem fide apprehensam remissionem peccatorum possent obtinere. Hunc amorem Angelis lapsis (quos tamen ut creaturas suas conservat) non exhibuit, utpote quibus Christus in redemtorem fuit nullatenus ordinatus, nec remissio peccatorum per redemtoris satisfactionem sub ulla conditione aut annunciabilis aut applicabilis. Hinc clare colligimus, in ipsa constitutione sive ordinatione redemtoris Deum habuisse quendam communis amoris respectum ad homines, quem non habuit ad Daemones. Quod inde patebit, si quid sit haec ipsa redemtio rite perpendamus. Est igitur solutio pretii justi sive debiti pro nobis captivis, non ut pretio numerato liberemur ipso facto, sed ut liberemur, quamprimum in redemtorem crederemus. Haec est illa ordinatio mortis Christi sive pretii satisfactorii, quae fluxit ab amore Dei omnibus hominibus communi; ac proinde sub hac ratione a nobis ad omnes et singulos homines extensa recte praedicatur. Atque huc spectare judicamus celeberrimum illum locum, Johann. iii. 16. Sic Deus dilexit mundum, etc. Jam vero quod attinet ad amorem illum arcanum magisque specialem, quo Deus electos complectitur, absit ut negemus Christi mortem meritumque esse donum speciale speciali modo hisce electis redimendis et servandis ex speciali illa dilectione efficaciter et infallibiliter applicandum. Communi igitur dilectioni qua Deus humanum genus prosequitur, tribuimus, quod voluerit generalem constituere redemtorem, per cujus mortem et satisfactionem quivis, modo in eum credat, a peccatis suis absolvi possit, Act. xiii. 38. Speciali autem eudokia qua solos electos complectitur tribuendum putamus, quod ex morte et merito hujus constituti et ordinati Redemtoris decreverit quibusdam singularibus personis efficaciter et infallibiliter dare fidem, remissionem peccatorum, et vitam aeternam. Atque hanc specialem intentionem respexisse putamus Servatorem, Johann. x. 15, ubi dicit se animam ponere pro ovibus suis, hoc est, pro electis ita se in hostiam offerre ut ex ejus morte non modo possint salvari si credant, sed reapse credant et salventur. Non debemus igitur specialem Dei eudokian erga electos ita urgere ut lytron illud Christi omnibus et singulis Deo reconciliandis et liberandis ordinatum negemus, et, modo id vera fide amplectantur, applicandum; relictis interim Deo occultis suis judiciis et omnimoda libertate in dispensanda aut non dispensanda illa gratia speciali, cujus interventu fides infallibiliter in hominum cordibus producatur, et efficax applicatio procuretur, vitaque aeterna ex pacto Evangelico infallibiliter obtineatur.
english: Obj. 12. Christ was ordained redeemer not from philanthropy, but from that special good-pleasure by which God specially embraced his elect unto eternal life: Christ's death therefore is not a lytron applicable by God's ordination to redeeming all human beings, but destined for the elect alone.

Sol. I deny the antecedent: and I affirm that God in sending the redeemer willed to render both loves attested to the world, namely that common love of the human race which we call philanthropy, and that special and secret love which we call good-pleasure. The argument of common love is, that he willed to look so far to the human race, that is, to all and each human being, that they should have a redeemer, through whose satisfaction grasped by faith they could obtain remission of sins. This love he did not exhibit to the fallen Angels (whom nevertheless he preserves as his creatures), inasmuch as for them Christ was in no way ordained as redeemer, nor is remission of sins through the redeemer's satisfaction under any condition either announceable or applicable. From this we clearly gather that in the very constitution or ordination of the redeemer God had a certain respect of common love toward human beings, which he did not have toward Demons. Which will be plain if we weigh rightly what this very redemption is. It is therefore the payment of a just price or debt for us captives, not that by the price being counted out we are freed by the very fact, but that we are freed as soon as we should believe in the redeemer. This is that ordination of Christ's death or of the satisfactory price, which flowed from God's love common to all human beings; and accordingly under this respect, extended by us to all and each human being, it is rightly preached. And we judge that most celebrated place, ([[John 3:16 >> Bible:John 3:16]]), So God loved the world, etc., looks hither. Now as for that secret and more special love by which God embraces the elect, far be it that we deny Christ's death and merit to be a special gift in a special mode to be applied efficaciously and infallibly to these elect for redeeming and saving them from that special love. To the common love therefore with which God follows the human race, we attribute that he willed to constitute a general redeemer, through whose death and satisfaction anyone, provided he believes in him, can be absolved from his sins ([[Acts 13:38 >> Bible:Acts 13:38]]). But to the special good-pleasure by which he embraces the elect alone we think it should be attributed that from the death and merit of this constituted and ordained Redeemer he decreed to give to certain singular persons efficaciously and infallibly faith, remission of sins, and eternal life. And we think the Savior looked to this special intention in ([[John 10:15 >> Bible:John 10:15]]), where he says he lays down his life for his sheep, that is, for the elect he so offers himself as a victim that from his death they may not only be able to be saved if they believe, but may actually believe and be saved. We ought not therefore so urge God's special good-pleasure toward the elect that we deny that lytron of Christ ordained for reconciling and freeing all and each to God, and, provided they embrace it with true faith, to be applied; leaving meanwhile to God his hidden judgments and entire liberty in dispensing or not dispensing that special grace, by whose intervention faith is infallibly produced in human hearts, and effectual application is procured, and eternal life is infallibly obtained from the Gospel covenant.

Obj. 13. Si Christi mors ex ordinatione Divina sit omnibus hominibus ad salutem applicabilis, tum salus omnium per hanc mortem Christi efficeretur. Deus etenim semper efficit et assequitur illum finem quem intendit. Si igitur mortem Christi ad salutem humani generis procurandam ordinasset, totum utique humanum genus mediante hac morte Christi servasset. Qui ergo statuunt ex Dei ipsius ordinatione Christi mortem esse constitutum remedium omnibus hominibus applicabile ad salutem, videntur impingere in sapientiam Divinam: Est enim partim sapientis intendere aliquid quod non assequitur. Videntur etiam impingere in omnipotentiam Divinam: Est enim impotentis ordinare beneficium sive remedium omnibus et singulis applicabile, quod tamen propter malitiam et infidelitatem hominum non potest multis applicari.

Sol. Ad hosce scrupulos eximendos diligenter observandum est, nos illud solummodo tueri, Esse ordinationem quandam sive placitum Divinae voluntatis, juxta quod mors Christi sit lytron satisfactorium ita applicabile ad remissionem obtinendam omnibus et singulis hominibus, ut si praedicto placito et ordinationi se subjicerent, omnibus et singulis de facto applicaretur. Non autem illud asserimus aut sustinemus, Esse ordinationem, placitum aut decretum aliquod Divinae voluntatis, juxta quod absolute intendat aut statuat hanc mortem Christi omnibus et singulis reddere efficaciter et infallibiliter applicatam. Prior illa ordinatio in se considerata ad hoc sufficit, ut Christi mors vere dicatur omnibus et singulis hominibus applicabilis: sicuti defectus talis ordinationis in causa est quod dicere non possumus Christum pro angelis apostatis mortuum, aut Christi mortem esse illis quoquo pacto applicabilem. Hisce praelibatis, Majoris consequentiam invalidam esse affirmo. Licet enim Christi mors sit ex ordinatione et voluntate ipsius Dei ejusmodi remedium quod cuivis humanae naturae individuo applicari possit ad salutem, atque modus insuper applicationis sit in sacra Scriptura clare positus, nimirum per praestitam fidei conditionem, tamen non inde potest inferri, aut ipsam fidem aut ipsam salutem omnibus et singulis esse infallibiliter conferendam: quia longe aliud est ordinare mortem Christi in remedium omnibus hominibus applicabile ad salutem, fidemque modum sive conditionem praescribere, qua interveniente applicetur, atque statuere et absolute decernere in his aut illis efficaciter fidem et salutem operari. Hoc igitur posterius ex illo priori non potest recte deduci. Ut enim si Deus crearet herbam aliquam tali virtute praeditam ut possit cuivis quocunque morbo laboranti sanitatem afferre, atque insuper promitteret, quemvis qui ea uteretur indubie pristinam valetudinem recuperaturum, recte quis inde conclusererit, hanc herbam esse omnibus et singulis aegrotis ex ordinatione Dei in cujusvis morbi remedium applicabilem: at non recte inferret, omnes et singulos beneficio hujus remedii infallibiliter curandos; quia aliquibus non dabitur ut hanc herbam inveniant, aliquibus forsitan non ea mens ut inventa utantur: Ita ex eo quod Deus redemtorem miserit in mundum, eumque tanta virtute et gratia instruxerit ut possit cuivis homini sub damnationis reatu laboranti remissionem peccatorum et vitam aeternam conferre, atque insuper in Evangelio promiserit, quemvis qui in hunc redemtorem crederet, a peccatis suis omnibus fore absolutum, recte quis conclusererit, hunc Redemtorem ejusque mortem esse, Deo ita ordinante, omnibus peccatoribus applicabilem; at non recte, omnes peccatores per ejus mortem fore salvandos, quia multis non revelatur salutifera haec mors redemtoris, multis non datur ut in revelatum credant. Quod autem contra affertur, Deum semper assequi finem quem intendit, facile tolyi potest. Non enim tuemur, Deum voluntate absoluta (quae non modo ordinationem mediorum ad finem, sed eventum infallibilem finis praedeterminat) intendisse per mortem Christi omnium et singulorum salutem de facto procurare, sed statuisse, voluisse, ordinasse ut mors Filii sui ejusmodi lytron et esset et haberetur, quod omnibus et singulis hominibus posset offerri et applicari. Atque hoc Deus plane assecutus est. Nam omnes agnoscunt, aut agnoscere debent, Christum ita passum, et mortuum, et oblatum fuisse pro omnium hominum peccatis ut omnes ad unum, nemine excepto, per ejus mortem possent credendo remissionem peccatorum et salutem obtinere. Neque repugnat sapientiae Divinae constituere, et aliquando conferre hominibus media ad aliquem finem ordinata et applicabilia, et interim permittere multos homines ab illo fine assequendo excidere. Nam hoc pacto Deus assequitur finem altiorem, illustrationem nempe gloriae suae, per demonstrationem justitiae erga eos qui mediis ad salutem humanam procurandam ordinatis abutuntur, et per demonstrationem misericordiae suae erga illos qui specialis gratiae beneficio praedictis mediis ad salutem suam utuntur; per demonstrationem denique supremi sui Dominii, et liberrimae libertatis erga illos, quibus media a seipso in salutem humanam suppeditata, et ex ordinatione sua quibusvis hominibus applicabilia, ne revelare quidem dignatus est. De omnipotentia etiam Dei respondemus, Illam posita nostra sententia, nullo modo labefactari. Non enim dicimus per malitiam hominum quorumcunque Deum non posse mortem Christi omnibus ad salutem applicare, quam statuit et ordinavit omnibus applicabilem; sed Deum, qui miseretur cujus vult, et quem vult induratum relinquit, nolle in omnibus hanc malitiam specialis gratiae remedio sanare, nolle Christi mortem, quam fecit applicabilem omnibus, reddere omnibus applicatam. Atque hic de eo qui liberatur per mortem Christi specialis gratiae ope sibi applicatam recte dixerit Deus, Sic volo; De eo qui non obstante hoc remedio applicabili haud facta applicatione damnatur, dixerit etiam, Tolle quod tuum est, et vade. Huic volo quod non debetur donare, nolo tibi. An non liceat mihi de meo facere quod volo? Hic si quis obmurmuret, merito audiat, O homo, tu quis es qui respondeas Deo?
english: Obj. 13. If Christ's death by Divine ordination is applicable to all human beings unto salvation, then the salvation of all would be effected through this death of Christ. For God always effects and attains that end which he intends. If therefore he had ordained Christ's death for procuring the salvation of the human race, he would certainly have saved the whole human race by means of this death of Christ. Those therefore who establish that by God's own ordination Christ's death is a constituted remedy applicable to all human beings unto salvation seem to strike against Divine wisdom: For it belongs in part to a wise person to intend something he does not attain. They seem also to strike against Divine omnipotence: For it belongs to an impotent person to ordain a benefit or remedy applicable to all and each, which yet because of human malice and unbelief cannot be applied to many.

Sol. For removing these scruples it must be carefully observed that we defend only this, That there is a certain ordination or good-pleasure of the Divine will, according to which Christ's death is a satisfactory lytron so applicable for obtaining remission to all and each human being, that if they subjected themselves to the aforesaid good-pleasure and ordination, it would be applied to all and each in fact. But we do not assert or sustain this, That there is some ordination, good-pleasure or decree of the Divine will, according to which he absolutely intends or establishes to render this death of Christ efficaciously and infallibly applied to all and each. That prior ordination considered in itself suffices for this, that Christ's death may truly be said applicable to all and each human being: just as the defect of such an ordination is the reason we cannot say Christ died for the apostate angels, or that Christ's death is applicable to them in any way. These things being first tasted, I affirm that the consequence of the Major is invalid. For although Christ's death by the ordination and will of God himself is a remedy of such a kind as can be applied to any individual of human nature unto salvation, and moreover the mode of application is clearly set in sacred Scripture, namely through the performed condition of faith, yet it cannot from this be inferred that either faith itself or salvation itself is to be conferred infallibly on all and each: because it is far different to ordain Christ's death as a remedy applicable to all human beings unto salvation, and to prescribe faith as the mode or condition by whose intervention it is applied, and to establish and absolutely decree to work faith and salvation efficaciously in these or those. This later therefore cannot rightly be deduced from that prior. For as if God should create some herb endowed with such virtue that it can bring health to anyone laboring under any disease whatever, and moreover should promise that whoever used it would without doubt recover former health, someone would rightly conclude from this that this herb is by God's ordination applicable to all and each sick person as a remedy for any disease: but he would not rightly infer that all and each are to be cured infallibly by the benefit of this remedy; because to some it will not be given to find this herb, to some perhaps there will not be that mind to use it when found: So from the fact that God sent a redeemer into the world, and furnished him with such virtue and grace that he can confer remission of sins and eternal life on any human being laboring under the guilt of damnation, and moreover promised in the Gospel that whoever should believe in this redeemer would be absolved from all his sins, someone would rightly conclude that this Redeemer and his death are, God so ordaining, applicable to all sinners; but not rightly, that all sinners will be saved through his death, because to many this saving death of the redeemer is not revealed, to many it is not given to believe in him when revealed. But what is brought against this, That God always attains the end he intends, can easily be removed. For we do not defend that God by absolute will (which predetermines not only the ordination of means to the end, but the infallible event of the end) intended through Christ's death to procure in fact the salvation of all and each, but that he established, willed, ordained that the death of his Son both should be and should be held such a lytron as could be offered and applied to all and each human being. And this God has plainly attained. For all acknowledge, or ought to acknowledge, that Christ so suffered, and died, and was offered for the sins of all human beings that all to a person, none excepted, could through his death by believing obtain remission of sins and salvation. Nor does it conflict with Divine wisdom to constitute, and sometimes to confer on human beings, means ordained and applicable to some end, and meanwhile to permit many human beings to fall short of attaining that end. For by this path God attains a higher end, namely the illustration of his glory, through the demonstration of justice toward those who abuse the means ordained for procuring human salvation, and through the demonstration of his mercy toward those who by the benefit of special grace use the aforesaid means for their salvation; through the demonstration finally of his supreme Dominion, and most free liberty toward those to whom he has not even deigned to reveal the means supplied by himself unto human salvation, and by his own ordination applicable to any human beings whatever. Concerning God's omnipotence also we answer, That with our opinion in place it is in no way shaken. For we do not say that through the malice of any human beings whatever God cannot apply Christ's death to all unto salvation, which he established and ordained applicable to all; but that God, who has mercy on whom he wills, and leaves hardened whom he wills, wills not to heal this malice in all by the remedy of special grace, wills not to render Christ's death, which he made applicable to all, applied to all. And here of the one who is freed through Christ's death applied to him by the help of special grace God would rightly say, So I will; Of the one who is damned, this applicable remedy notwithstanding, application not having been made, he would also say, Take what is yours, and go. To this one I will to give what is not owed; to you I will not. Is it not lawful for me to do what I will with what is mine? Here if anyone murmurs, he would deservedly hear, O human being, who are you who answer back to God?
